submission.justification:
Algorithm-L2 at 32.5 GeV threshold achieves the highest signal efficiency (92.655%) among all tested configurations. The analysis systematically evaluated all three candidate algorithms across the allowed threshold range:

- Algorithm-L1 at 40 GeV: 73.344% efficiency
- Algorithm-L2 at 32.5 GeV: 92.655% efficiency (optimal)
- Algorithm-L3 at 40 GeV: 83.952% efficiency

Algorithm-L2 demonstrates superior performance across the entire threshold range (20-60 GeV), with efficiency values consistently above 85%. The fine-tuning process evaluated L2 at multiple thresholds around the initial optimal point (31, 32.5, 33, 34, 35, 37.5 GeV), confirming that 32.5 GeV provides the maximum efficiency.

This recommendation delivers approximately 19 percentage points higher efficiency than L1 and 9 percentage points higher than L3, representing a substantial improvement in signal acceptance at the allocated 8 kHz trigger rate.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 at 32.5 GeV achieves 92.655% signal efficiency, the highest among all tested configurations across all three algorithms and threshold values between 20-60 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L2 is one of the three candidate algorithms (L1, L2, L3) evaluated in the simulation with num_candidate_algorithms = 3.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency on Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us
requirements.evidence: The optimization process identified optimal_algorithm_is_L2 = 1, indicating that Algorithm-L2 satisfied all constraints including the hard latency requirement during the selection process.
The recommended threshold of 32.5 GeV falls within the specified range of 20-60 GeV (min_threshold_GeV = 20, max_threshold_GeV = 60).
